review_findings: Slice I: the End key computed the film's total from segmentSecondsList(currentScriptData) instead of routing through timelineSeek, which opens with an empty-film guard. currentScriptData is null until a project loads and renderTimelineScreen explicitly supports that state ('no film loaded'), so pressing 3 then End on a fresh app threw TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'segments'). Reproduced, then fixed with if (!tlPictures().length) return;.

Slice I: timelineTogglePlay carried the same unguarded read below its !audio guard. <audio id='tl-audio'> is present in index.html, so the guard never fired and Space on an empty Timeline crashed the same way. Pre-existing rather than new, but one line from the same fix, and Slice I restructured that branch, so it was closed in the same commit. The guard sits below the pause branch so pausing still works with no film loaded.

Slice I's 8 tests are honest, unlike Slice G's and Slice H's: 11 of 12 independent mutations were caught. The one escape was the 3 key's container focus - test_3_stage_navigation only asserted switchPane('timeline') was called, so removing the focus hand-off changed nothing. Closed by test_key_3_focuses_timeline_container.
known_gaps: The three picture-boundary deltas from Slice H Job 3 were reported but not written to an artifact. If picture drift matters in Milestone 3, measure it again and record it.

The 1/2/3 and transport keys do not check ctrlKey/altKey/metaKey, so Ctrl+1 switches panes. The app binds no modifier shortcuts anywhere (grep for ctrlKey/metaKey/altKey returns nothing) and WebView2 has no tab bar to collide with, so this is cosmetic. Fix it the next time that listener is opened.
Slice I's keyboard work was verified through the Node DOM harness, not the live WebView2 window. Antigravity's Slice J verification gate should confirm the real keys fire.
